V6tn_note.R1: Strong crumbling-plaster walls and a good lane perspective. The soldiers are a dense, stiff, mannequin-like clump with similar poses. Some shading gives them a little volume. Tricorns, red and blue coats and cross-belts read as roughly 18th-century British.
V6tn_note.R2: Strong, convincing wall and rubble materials with a believable perspective and light. The soldiers are small, glossy, over-clean CG figures with a uniform pose and scale, and they are packed into one blob. The red and blue coats, white cross-belts and aimed muskets are plausible. The Union flag and sea at the end of the lane read well. The lane has far too little street life and no civilians.
V6tn_note.R3: Strong, believable ruined walls and raking light. The soldiers are small, uniformly lit, saturated and doll-like, packed into a tight clump with the same pose repeated. The left group is more varied and legible, with a drummer and an officer. The Union flag is tiny, and at this size the design can't be checked. The scale of the people against the buildings is slightly off.

V6sx_note.R1: The environment is identical to X. The soldiers are more saturated and flatter, like pasted cutouts or game sprites. The figures in the mid-lane are muddier and darker. The added barrel on the right is a small plus but doesn't fix the figures. Overall it looks slightly more game-asset than X.
V6sx_note.R2: The environment is the same as X. The figures are fewer, flatter and more saturated, like painted plastic miniatures. A few figures, such as the one at left with the yellow sash and the one at the barrel, have muddy, ill-defined shapes. The crowd is a dense cluster without depth. The barrel on the right adds a little clutter and does not help.
V6sx_note.R3: Same set and lighting as X. The left-hand figures are fewer and one has a smeared green-black face and torso, so it reads as a glitch. The figures look more like flat game-asset cutouts, with weaker silhouettes and a thinner crowd. An added barrel on the right is a small plus. The Union flag is the same tiny, unverifiable one.

why.R1: The walls and lighting are the same, but X's soldiers have slightly more volume and believable shading, while Y's look flatter and more like toy cutouts.
why.R2: The environment is nearly identical, but X has a slightly richer, better-shaded and more legible group of soldiers, while Y's figures look flatter, more plastic and more like toys.
why.R3: The environments are identical, but X's foreground soldiers are more varied and coherent, while Y has a malformed figure and a thinner, more toy-like group.

fix.R1: Break up the soldier block: fewer figures with varied poses, scale and spacing, plus grounded contact shadows, muted worn cloth colours and some dust or smoke haze so they sit in the lane. Also add small human clutter such as washing, a cart and a civilian or two.
fix.R2: Replace the flat, saturated figures with properly scaled, desaturated, varied soldiers (different poses, dirt and wear on the uniforms) with real contact shadows. Spread them along the lane in depth with a few civilians, smoke and haze, instead of one clump, and add period street props such as handcarts, water casks and shuttered stalls.
fix.R3: Redo the foreground soldiers: remove or regenerate the smeared green-faced figure, vary poses and spacing, and give them real shadows, contact grounding and scale-correct detail. Add smoke, dust or rubble interaction so they stop reading as pasted figures.

Modern-looking louvred or panelled shutters and neat rectangular door frames

V6sx_note.R1: The buildings are well lit and well textured. The crowd is smooth and mannequin-like, with hard silhouettes and little clothing or equipment detail. The figures read as game assets and look pasted onto the street. The Union Jack is tiny and the ship is a vague blur.
V6sx_note.R2: Strong, convincing architecture with peeling plaster, balconies and atmospheric haze. The crowd is the weak point. The figures are small, stiff, mannequin-like and lit flatly. Several are loosely scattered in the plaza and look like game assets. The sailors' white uniforms and the khaki figures are readable. A single-colour flat blue wall panel sits at the right, mid-distance. The Union Jack on a pole is tiny. A cannonball stack is visible at left.
V6sx_note.R3: Strong CGI street with convincing peeling plaster and balconies. The crowd is made of stiff, mannequin-like figures in pale, washed-out colours, with identical poses. Figures are lit flatly and don't match the scene's lighting. The foreground soldiers are plain, untextured shapes. The Union Jack on the pole is tiny, and the harbour and ship are generic.

V6tn_note.R1: The scene is identical, but the figures show a little more uniform and kit detail: webbing, packs and shading on the clothing. The crowd is still stiff and doll-like, and still a dense clump at mid-distance. The same weak flag and ship sit in the haze.
V6tn_note.R2: Environment is identical to X. The crowd is slightly denser and more overlapping, with rifles or sticks visible among the foreground soldiers, which reads a bit more like a populated scene. Figures are still stiff, mannequin-like and plastic. The dense cluster in the middle ground merges into a blob of heads with little individual silhouette. The foreground soldiers have more gear detail (webbing, rifles) than in X.
V6tn_note.R3: Same environment as X. The figures are slightly darker and more varied in uniform tone, and the foreground soldiers show some webbing and kit detail. They still look like game-asset mannequins, in clumped groups with stiff poses. Scale and grounding are slightly better, but it is still not convincing.

why.R1: The buildings and framing are the same, and Y's slightly better-defined figures make it read a bit less like mannequins.
why.R2: The environment is pixel-identical and the crowd differs only marginally: Y has a denser crowd with a bit more gear detail but muddier clustering, while X is cleaner but sparser, and both have the same mannequin look.
why.R3: The environments are identical, but Y's crowd has slightly more tonal variety and kit detail and looks a little less like toy figures.

fix.R1: Replace the smooth mannequin crowd with varied, properly textured figures in mixed poses and scales, then add contact shadows and foreground life such as carts, crates and a few civilians so the street doesn't look like a staged diorama.
fix.R2: Replace the stiff, evenly lit crowd with varied poses, contact shadows and scale-appropriate people with better skin and cloth shading. Break up the clumping with a few mid-ground groups and add motion blur or depth-of-field so the people sit inside the haze.
fix.R3: Re-render the crowd in X with varied poses and spacing, darker khaki and navy uniforms with proper shading, and contact shadows. Remove the identical pale figures so they stop reading as mannequins.
